ai.title: Add admin trace dashboard with interactive timeline visualization
ai.summary: New admin trace dashboard added to web package with interactive timeline visualization for debugging client sessions. Shared XML parsing utilities introduced in packages/internal/src/utils/xml-parser.ts for tool call/result extraction. Covers web/src/app/admin/traces/* components including timeline-chart, trace-viewer, client-session-viewer, and chat-message. Trace processing logic in web/src/app/admin/traces/utils/trace-processing.ts parses tool calls from content and extracts user/assistant messages.

eli5.text: A debugging interface was added to the internal admin web application that lets support staff replay and inspect individual client sessions as an interactive timeline of messages, tool calls, and responses. When you expand a session on the timeline you'll see a chat-style view of what the client and assistant said, with any tools the assistant decided to call shown as clickable references so you can trace the steps that led to a particular outcome. The change is live now in the admin tool and only affects internal staff who have access to these trace records; regular end users of the service are not impacted.

ai.title: Remove spawnableAgents field from agent registry
ai.summary: Removed `spawnableAgents` assignment in `AgentRegistry` within `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts`. The registry no longer injects the full list of agent types into base template objects. This simplifies the dynamic agent resolution logic by eliminating redundant state propagation.

eli5.text: The system has stopped injecting the full list of agent types into base template objects, simplifying the dynamic agent resolution logic. Internal tooling now skips injecting the spawnableAgents field into registry templates, so dynamic agents no longer carry the complete list of base types at startup. If you're building workflows that previously relied on the base template containing all spawnable agents, those templates will no longer include spawnableAgents as an embedded field.

ai.title: DynamicAgentService loads templates from fileContext paths
ai.summary: DynamicAgentService now uses full file paths from `fileContext.agentTemplates` instead of hardcoding `.agents/templates/` prefix. `loadAgents`, `collectAgentIds`, and `loadSingleAgent` pass `filePath` directly, removing `path.basename` stripping and manual `.agents/templates/${fileName}` reconstruction. Scope limited to `backend/src/templates/dynamic-agent-service.ts`. Ensures user-provided agent templates load correctly regardless of local `.agents/templates` directory presence.

eli5.text: Your custom project-specific agent templates now load reliably instead of going missing when a shared local template folder is present. Previously, the system ignored the full file paths you provided and rebuilt them from a fixed local folder prefix, which caused your templates to be skipped or misread. The system now uses the exact file paths you gave, so your own agent templates are loaded correctly regardless of what local template folders exist. This is live today and affects how project-defined agents are discovered and loaded.

ai.title: Restore user-defined agents to base template spawnableAgents
ai.summary: Fixes regression where user-defined agents were missing from base agent templates' `spawnableAgents`. `AgentRegistry` now explicitly merges `dynamicAgentService` types (excluding overrides) into static base templates. Affects backend `agent-registry.ts`.

eli5.text: Custom assistants you add yourself now show up again as options you can spawn from the main system assistants. The system accidentally stopped listing your custom assistants alongside the built-in ones when loading up the basic assistant types, and this puts them back on that list. You'll see your custom assistants appear as choices again when the system loads its default set of available assistants.
